newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. bank robber uses train in getaway.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. bank robber uses train in getaway.

text.p: An unemployed man robbed a bank Monday and when cornered while trying to escape on a train kept police at bay by holding a passenger hostage with a bag of books that he claimed was a bomb, police said.
Suffolk County Police Officer Thaddieus Nieves said the man surrendered without violence after the train was evacuated.

The man, identified by police as Anthony Norman, 34, of Brentwood, Long Island, walked into the European American Bank in Brentwood, New York, shortly after 10 a.m. EST, placed what he said was a bomb on the counter of the teller's window and demanded money.
The man raced from the bank with $2,000 and then got on a train.

After witnesses reported seeing the robber get on the train, police boarded it at the Wayandanch, N.Y. station, about 40 miles east of New York City, and confronted the suspect who then grabbed a passenger as a hostage, police said.
About 450 people on the train were evacuated as police negotiated release of the passenger. The suspect surrendered peacefully, police said.
"It turns out that Norman was unarmed and what he claimed was an explosive device was a bag of books," Nieves said.
